ga-nuong-sau-rieng-lai-thieu.name: Lai Thieu Durian-Roasted Chicken
ga-nuong-sau-rieng-lai-thieu.serving_basis: One roasted chicken, carved to share among four people.
ga-nuong-sau-rieng-lai-thieu.description: Chicken is marinated with ripe durian flesh and roasted until fragrant and golden, with gentle fruity richness. The dish is associated with the orchard area of Lai Thieu, Binh Duong; Bếp Việt standardizes the proportions for a family meal.
ga-nuong-sau-rieng-lai-thieu.finished_dish: Golden-brown skin and juicy meat carry a light, creamy sweetness from the durian without masking the chicken.
ga-nuong-sau-rieng-lai-thieu.serving: Rest for 8 minutes before carving. Serve with sticky or steamed rice, cucumber and herbs.
tips: Choose fragrant ripe durian and remove the seeds before mashing.
Marinate in the refrigerator; do not leave raw poultry at room temperature.
Use steady medium-hot coals and turn regularly so the durian does not burn; the thickest part should reach 74°C.
ga-nuong-sau-rieng-lai-thieu.image_alt: Lai Thieu durian-roasted chicken, golden brown with a light glaze and fresh herbs on a ceramic plate; original Bếp Việt image on transparency.
ga-nuong-sau-rieng-lai-thieu.time_note: About 3 hours 25 minutes, including a 2-hour marinade; roasting time depends on the chicken and equipment.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Adjust to the sweetness of the fruit.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Reduce if the durian is very sweet.

preparation_steps: Clean and pat the chicken dry. Lightly score the thickest parts of the thighs and breast.
Mix durian, shallot, garlic, fish sauce, sugar, oil and pepper. Set aside a clean spoonful for basting; rub the rest over the chicken and marinate, covered, in the refrigerator for 2 hours.
cooking_steps: Heat the oven to 180°C; take the chicken out of the refrigerator about 20 minutes before roasting.
Roast for 50–60 minutes, depending on size. Turn several times and brush with the reserved mixture.
Check that the thickest part reaches 74°C. Rest for 8 minutes, carve and serve.

ga-hap-buoi-tan-trieu.name: Tan Trieu Pomelo-Steamed Chicken
aliases: Chicken steamed in a Tan Trieu pomelo
ga-hap-buoi-tan-trieu.serving_basis: Free-range chicken steamed in a pomelo shell, shared by four people.
ga-hap-buoi-tan-trieu.description: Seasoned chicken is placed inside a hollowed Tan Trieu pomelo and steamed with pomelo leaves. The steam carries the aroma of the rind into the meat, making this a distinctive dish of the Tan Trieu pomelo-growing area in Dong Nai.
ga-hap-buoi-tan-trieu.finished_dish: Tender, juicy chicken scented with pomelo oils and a faintly bitter, fresh finish.
ga-hap-buoi-tan-trieu.serving: Serve hot with lime-pepper salt or ginger fish sauce, fresh vegetables and steamed rice.
tips: Choose a ripe but firm pomelo with a thick, unbroken rind; hollow it carefully.
Use pomelo leaves sparingly and avoid over-steaming, since the essential oils can turn bitter.
Arrange the chicken loosely so steam can circulate; the thickest part should reach 74°C.
ga-hap-buoi-tan-trieu.image_alt: Tan Trieu pomelo-steamed chicken in an opened pomelo shell with pomelo leaves; original Bếp Việt image on transparency.
ga-hap-buoi-tan-trieu.time_note: About 1 hour 50 minutes, including a 30-minute marinade; steam for 35–45 minutes depending on the pieces.

ingredients.name: Free-range chicken pieces
ingredients.notes: Cut small enough to fit inside the pomelo.

ingredients.name: Tan Trieu pomelo
ingredients.notes: Choose a large fruit; hollow it while keeping the rind intact.

ingredients.name: Pomelo leaves
ingredients.notes: Shred some and use the rest to line the steamer.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Use a small amount to balance seasoning.

preparation_steps: Rinse and drain the chicken, then cut into bite-sized pieces. Mix with shallot, garlic, pomelo wine, fish sauce, salt, sugar and pepper; marinate in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Cut off the pomelo top to make a lid. Scoop out the flesh while preserving the rind as a steaming vessel; rinse the leaves and line the bottom with some.
cooking_steps: Arrange the chicken and shredded pomelo leaves inside the shell, replace the lid and set it in a steamer over gently boiling water.
Steam for 35–45 minutes, depending on piece size. Check that the thickest part reaches 74°C; avoid over-steaming.
Carefully remove the pomelo, open it while hot and serve with lime-pepper salt.

com-ga-ca-man-long-khanh.name: Long Khanh Chicken and Salted-Fish Rice
aliases: Long Khanh chicken and salted-fish fried rice
Dong Nai chicken and salted-fish rice
com-ga-ca-man-long-khanh.serving_basis: One pan of chicken and salted-fish rice as a main dish for four.
com-ga-ca-man-long-khanh.description: Cooled rice is stir-fried with shredded chicken and roasted, flaked salted fish. The combination makes a savory rice dish associated with Long Khanh, Dong Nai; Bếp Việt edits the proportions for a home meal.
com-ga-ca-man-long-khanh.finished_dish: Separate grains fragrant with salted fish and aromatics, with soft shredded chicken and a balanced savory taste.
com-ga-ca-man-long-khanh.serving: Serve hot with cucumber, tomato or blanched greens.
tips: Cook the rice slightly dry and cool it completely; warm, moist rice can become sticky.
Salted fish can be very salty. Taste it before adding fish sauce or salt.
Stir-fry the fish and chicken first, then add the rice over fairly high heat; cook in batches if needed.
search_terms: Long Khanh chicken salted fish rice
Dong Nai chicken salted fish fried rice
com-ga-ca-man-long-khanh.image_alt: Long Khanh chicken and salted-fish rice with separate grains, shredded chicken, roasted salted fish and scallion; original Bếp Việt image on transparency.
com-ga-ca-man-long-khanh.time_note: About 1 hour 20 minutes if cooking fresh rice; less when pre-cooked rice is ready.

ingredients.name: Rice
ingredients.notes: Cook with slightly less water so the grains stay separate.

ingredients.name: Salted fish
ingredients.notes: Roast or pan-cook, remove bones and flake; adjust to saltiness.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Add only after tasting the fish.

preparation_steps: Cook the rice slightly dry. Spread it on a tray to cool, then gently separate the grains.
Poach the chicken until just cooked, cool slightly and shred. Roast or pan-cook the salted fish until fragrant, remove bones and flake.
cooking_steps: Sauté shallot and garlic in some oil. Add salted fish and stir until fragrant, then add chicken and scallion whites.
Add cooled rice and stir-fry over medium-high heat until separate and hot. Season with pepper; add fish sauce only after tasting.
When the grains are dry and evenly heated, fold in the scallion greens and remove from the heat. Serve at once.

vit-nau-tieu-xanh-mien-tay.name: Mekong-Style Duck Stew with Green Peppercorns
aliases: Green peppercorn duck and potato stew
vit-nau-tieu-xanh-mien-tay.serving_basis: One pot of green peppercorn duck and potatoes for four.
vit-nau-tieu-xanh-mien-tay.description: Duck is marinated, browned, then simmered with potatoes, lemongrass and green peppercorns until tender. The dish has been shared as part of Mekong Delta family feasts; this is Bếp Việt's home-style version.
vit-nau-tieu-xanh-mien-tay.finished_dish: Tender but intact duck pieces, potatoes steeped in a peppery broth, and fragrant green peppercorns.
vit-nau-tieu-xanh-mien-tay.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice or bread, with fresh vegetables if desired.
tips: Rub duck with ginger and salt or a little rice wine to reduce odor, then rinse and pat dry.
Add potatoes after the duck has started to tenderize so they do not fall apart.
Add green peppercorns in two stages to retain some fresh aroma.
vit-nau-tieu-xanh-mien-tay.image_alt: Mekong-style green peppercorn duck with tender pieces, potatoes and peppercorn sprigs in an earthenware pot; original Bếp Việt image on transparency.
vit-nau-tieu-xanh-mien-tay.time_note: About 2 hours, including a 30-minute marinade; simmering time varies with the duck.

ingredients.name: Cleaned duck
ingredients.notes: Cut into bite-sized pieces; choose a not-too-old duck.

ingredients.name: Green peppercorns
ingredients.notes: Rinse; leave some whole and lightly crush some.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.notes: Peel and cut into large chunks.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Divide between marinade and final seasoning.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Add just to cover; adjust as needed.

preparation_steps: Rub duck with salt and ginger, rinse, pat dry and cut into pieces. Marinate with half the fish sauce, sugar, shallot, garlic and a little peppercorn for 30 minutes.
Rinse remaining peppercorns and lightly crush some. Prepare potatoes, onion and lemongrass.
cooking_steps: Sauté lemongrass with the remaining shallot and garlic. Add duck and brown on all sides.
Add enough water to barely cover, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for about 35 minutes or until nearly tender.
Add potatoes, onion and remaining peppercorns; simmer another 15–20 minutes until cooked. Adjust seasoning and serve hot.

vit-khia-nuoc-dua-mien-tay.name: Mekong-Style Duck Braised in Coconut Water
vit-khia-nuoc-dua-mien-tay.serving_basis: One pot of coconut-braised duck to serve with rice for four.
vit-khia-nuoc-dua-mien-tay.description: Duck is seasoned, browned, then gently braised in coconut water until tender and coated in a glossy reduction. This rustic method is commonly presented in Mekong Delta cooking; Bếp Việt adapts the seasoning for a family meal.
vit-khia-nuoc-dua-mien-tay.finished_dish: Tender duck infused with coconut water and seasoning, coated in glossy brown sauce with a balanced sweet-savory taste.
vit-khia-nuoc-dua-mien-tay.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice, cucumber or fresh greens; spoon a little sauce over the rice.
tips: Clean the duck with ginger and salt, rinse thoroughly and pat dry.
Brown the skin side first so the duck renders fat and develops color; pour off excess fat if needed.
Braise over low heat and uncover near the end to reduce the sauce. Taste before reducing because both sauces are salty.
vit-khia-nuoc-dua-mien-tay.image_alt: Mekong-style coconut-braised duck with glossy brown pieces in reduced coconut sauce and scallion; original Bếp Việt image on transparency.
vit-khia-nuoc-dua-mien-tay.time_note: About 1 hour 50 minutes, including a 30-minute marinade; braising time depends on piece size.

ingredients.name: Cleaned duck
ingredients.notes: Cut into bite-sized pieces and drain.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: Use some to clean the duck and slice the rest.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Adjust after tasting the soy sauce.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Balance the coconut water to taste.

ingredients.name: Neutral oil
ingredients.notes: Use for searing if the duck is lean.

preparation_steps: Rub duck with salt and ginger, rinse, drain and cut into pieces. Mix with shallot, garlic, soy sauce, some fish sauce, sugar and pepper; cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Prepare coconut water and slice the ginger. Set aside a clean spoonful of marinade before mixing it with raw duck, in case the sauce needs adjustment.
cooking_steps: Heat a heavy pot and sear duck until lightly browned on all sides; pour off excess fat if needed.
Add the remaining marinade, coconut water and ginger. Bring to a boil, lower heat and braise for 40–50 minutes, turning the pieces several times.
When the duck is tender and sauce glossy, taste and adjust fish sauce or sugar. Garnish with scallion and pepper, then serve hot.
